blocks.md: This Yu-Gi-Oh! Genesys tier list ranks the strongest decks on the YGO Omega Genesys ladder by their results, using data through November 2, 2026. **Synchron / Kewl Tune** (0.6% of the meta, expected 58.4%), **Artmage / Elfnote** (0.9% of the meta, expected 58.0%), **Angelechy / Ashtra** (1.2% of the meta, expected 57.9%), **Angelechy** (1.8% of the meta, expected 57.0%), **Blitzclique** (5.4% of the meta, expected 56.3%), **Angelechy / Centur-Ion** (0.8% of the meta, expected 56.2%), **Angelechy / Eldlich** (0.7% of the meta, expected 56.1%), **Angelechy / White Forest** (1.4% of the meta, expected 56.0%) and **Blitzclique / Rescue-ACE** (0.8% of the meta, expected 55.7%) share Tier 1.

blocks.caption: The Genesys tier list at a glance

blocks.md: A tier here measures **how well a deck wins**, not how much it is played, and a small sample can't lift a deck to the top. For what moved this week, read the [latest meta report](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-meta-report-november-3-2026); for the other ladder, the [TCG tier list](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-tcg-tier-list); for the numbers as they change, the [live statistics page](/statistics?ladder=genesys).

The Genesys ladder is 44 days into the 09.2026 season, with 25,655 games from 1,509 players. The most played deck, Blitzclique, holds 5.4% of the meta, and the 22 decks in these tiers cover 26% of it. New to the format? The [format primer](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-formats) explains the 100-point rule.

blocks.text: Which decks are underplayed and overplayed?

blocks.md:
Popularity and results don't always agree. The underplayed decks reach Tier 2 or better on a small share of the meta, though the people playing them may be specialists, so treat them as leads to test. The overplayed decks are among the ten most played without reaching Tier 2.

- **Underplayed:** Angelechy / Rescue-ACE (0.5% of the meta, expected 55.0%), Synchron / Kewl Tune (0.6% of the meta, expected 58.4%) and Angelechy / Eldlich (0.7% of the meta, expected 56.1%)
- **Overplayed:** HERO (2.9% of the meta, expected 48.9%), Darklord / Artmage (2.5% of the meta, expected 48.8%) and Dracotail / Predap (2.5% of the meta, expected 49.1%)

Best and worst matchup for each top deck against Tiers 1 to 3. A matchup is listed only when its 95% interval excludes the rate the two decks' strengths predict, with at least 80 games.

| Deck | Best matchup | Worst matchup |
|---|---|---|
| **Synchron / Kewl Tune** | None clear | None clear |
| **Artmage / Elfnote** | None clear | None clear |
| **Angelechy / Ashtra** | None clear | None clear |
| **Angelechy** | None clear | None clear |
| **Blitzclique** | None clear | None clear |
| **Angelechy / Centur-Ion** | None clear | None clear |

Every number comes from ranked games played on [YGO Omega](/wiki/ygo-omega-wiki), the same data behind our [statistics page](/statistics?ladder=genesys). Nothing is voted on or picked by hand.

These are **power tiers**: they rank results, and the statistics page shows the same tiers.

**Each deck gets an expected win rate.** One model reads the games of the season between players rated Silver and up, after leaving out players with too few ranked games and one-off decklists: each deck has a strength, and the chance of winning depends on the two strengths, on who went first and on the rating gap. A deck's expected win rate is its strength against the whole field, weighted by how much each deck is played, and a deck with few games is pulled toward the middle. A tier reads that rate against fixed marks:

| Tier | Expected win rate |
|---|---|
| Tier 1 | 55% or more |
| Tier 1.5 | 54% or more |
| Tier 2 | 52.5% or more |
| Tier 3 | 51% or more |
| Tier 4 | 50% or more |

Decks under the last mark stay outside the tiers. A deck needs at least 0.5% of the meta and 10 players to be ranked at all, because the model corrects for few games, not for few pilots.

- **Meta share** is the deck's share of deck-games. Each game counts once per player, and mirror matches count.
- **The 95% interval** is the range the expected win rate is likely in, widened by how much the deck's daily results move beyond chance.
- **Decks** are grouped by the archetypes they run, so a hybrid counts apart from pure builds.

blocks.title: What this list can't tell you
blocks.md: This is ladder play on a simulator, not tournament results. Players of every level are in it, and a deck played mostly by specialists can score above what it would do in most hands. It shows what wins on the ladder, which is not always what wins a premier event.

items.q: What is the best Genesys deck right now?
items.md: Synchron / Kewl Tune, with an expected 58.4% win rate (95% interval 53.1–63.5) at 0.6% of the meta.

items.q: Is this tier list based on tournament results?
items.md: No. It comes from ranked ladder games on YGO Omega. That gives a far larger sample than tournaments, but it reflects ladder play, not premier events.
By expected win rate against the field: Tier 1 from 55%, Tier 1.5 from 54%, Tier 2 from 52.5%, Tier 3 from 51%, Tier 4 from 50%. Decks under 0.5% of the meta or 10 players aren't ranked.

items.q: Does a popular deck get a higher tier?
items.md: No. Tiers follow results. HERO holds 2.9% of the meta and sits outside the tiers, while Angelechy / Rescue-ACE holds 0.5% and sits in Tier 1.5.

items.q: How much does going first matter?
items.md: Going first wins 64.9% of game 1 between even decks on the Genesys ladder.

items.q: How often is the tier list updated?
items.md: Every week, on this same page. Each week also gets its own [meta report](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-meta-report-november-3-2026), and the [statistics page](/statistics?ladder=genesys) shows the current numbers between updates.

items.q: Where can I see decklists for these decks?
items.md: The [statistics page](/statistics?ladder=genesys) has sample decklists, card usage and full matchup tables for each deck.
